statement: The first line holds a string s of lowercase letters; the second holds k. Print the length of the longest substring containing at most k distinct characters. Slide a window with a 26-slot count table and a live distinct counter: an entering character that brings its count from 0 to 1 raises distinct; while distinct exceeds k, advance the left end, and a count falling back to 0 lowers distinct. Offer the width as a candidate only while the window is valid.

example.why: cbebebe holds exactly the three kinds c, b and e; every longer substring holds four.

hint: Keep distinct as a number maintained on zero-crossings; re-scanning the table each step wastes 26.
mistake: Measuring the window while distinct still exceeds k - mid-repair widths are phantoms.
